The source pack begins directly with the header of table 4; the body of the alate description (text page) is not included, only its comparison sentence with F. brevilabius, so no separate Alate section is given. OCR problem: in the soldier measurement table (table 5) the figures of every column are completely out of register with the names of the measurements and cannot be matched reliably, so they are not recorded; figure and table numbers follow the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate (the neotype queen): smaller than F. brevilabius in all measurements and paler in colour, the T-shaped mark on the pronotum lighter and more distinct; frontal gland pore larger, its depression shallower; pronotum only slightly longer than half its width. Soldier distinguished from the other species as follows: F. parviceps has a shorter head, a generally smaller body, less convergent sides of the anterior part of the head and a narrower frontal projection in dorsal view, while the proportions of the postmentum, labrum and mandibles are similar; F. longilabius has a longer median lobe of the labrum and slightly more curved lateral margins of the labrum; F. brevilabius has a shorter median lobe of the labrum and more curved lateral margins of the labrum; F. brevimalatus is smaller, with short mandibles and curved lateral margins of the labrum; F. soyerti has a shorter head, thinner and shorter mandibles, and a thicker labral lobe with more curved lateral margins; F. hendrickxi has shorter lateral lobes of the labrum and slightly different measurements; F. cubitalis has more strongly elbowed mandibles and a deeper concavity of the head surface behind the frontal projection in lateral view.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Vertex in lateral view almost straight or slightly concave (slightly convex in one case). The most conspicuous diagnostic features of the species are the sizes and proportions of the parts, the shape of the labrum (fig. 9A) and the shape of the mandibles (fig. 8A). Antennae 14 or 15-segmented. In some specimens the outline of the mandibles is slightly less regular than in fig. 8A, but the outer margin is fairly evenly convex in all of them, not elbowed (the latter occurs in F. cubitalis, fig. 9C).
